page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.32xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 7H12 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz, providing a total of 128 dedicated vCPUs. It incorporates 512.0 GB of system memory, which maintains a standard balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Network infrastructure capabilities include a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps. The instance provides no integrated local storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring all persistent storage and public network routing to be attached externally via cloud storage volumes and network interfaces. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs provisioned on this configuration.

This hardware footprint emphasizes high concurrency and resource density, allowing large workloads to operate across 128 compute cores without sharing CPU cycles with neighboring tenants. From an efficiency perspective, the balanced memory-to-vCPU allocation supports high resource utilization for compute environments that do not require dedicated NVMe solid-state storage or specialized hardware acceleration.

Appropriate deployments for ecs.g6a.32xlarge include large enterprise web backends, distributed data processing pipelines, enterprise resource planning applications, container cluster worker nodes, and distributed cache or database clusters that operate over networked block storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.32xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor. Featuring 128 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz alongside 512.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Network throughput is provisioned with a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration omits local disk storage and GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for persistent data. This resource distribution makes the instance effective for highly concurrent enterprise workloads that demand substantial parallel processing and memory density, such as distributed application servers, large container orchestration platforms, batch data processing, and multi-tenant hosting environments without dedicated accelerator requirements.
